solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Part of shoe Alf's found in cavity

indicators.note: something found in another thing sits inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: a cavity is a hole
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone called Alf has a gap in the bottom of his shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cavity' might suggest a tooth, but it is simply a hole that wraps the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-sole is the replacement piece fitted to the front part of a shoe's underside during repair.

clue.text: Headwear husband owns no longer

definitions.note: 'no longer' marks an archaic form: hath is the old third-person form of has

blocks.note: a hat is headwear
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband who once had a hat no longer possesses it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' seems to say he has lost the hat, but it marks the old-fashioned word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hath is the archaic form of has, so it means possesses in a form no longer in use.

clue.text: Undeveloped creature right inside molten rock

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: lava is molten rock from a volcano
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A primitive creature survives inside a volcano's flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the immature form of an insect before metamorphosis, so not yet developed.

clue.text: Editor in Times, reflecting, longed for certain type of house

indicators.note: in places the word before it inside the newspaper name that follows
a reflection shows things mirrored, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor, thinking back, yearned for a particular kind of home.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion happens first and the reversal then turns the whole newspaper name round, editor included.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-detached house shares one wall with its neighbour, a common British style of home.

clue.text: Casual about occasionally fraying part of body

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only alternate letters are kept
about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: lax means casual or careless
second, fourth and sixth letters of fraying

explanation.surface: Someone careless about a piece of their body coming apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The larynx, or voice box, is an organ in the throat, a part of the human body.

clue.text: Audibly milk sheep

indicators.note: audibly tells you to go by how a word is heard when spoken rather than how it is written

blocks.note: to milk a situation is to use or exploit it

explanation.surface: An instruction to milk sheep noisily, as on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milk' looks like something done to sheep, but here it means exploit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewes are female sheep, so the plural noun names sheep generally enough to stand in.

clue.text: Wife remains, contrary to expectation, lifting cleaning vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting sends the word upwards, so it is read bottom to top

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
ash is what remains after burning
but introduces something contrary to what was expected

explanation.surface: Unexpectedly, the wife is still there, picking up the laundry tub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' reads as a verb about the wife, but it is the noun for leftovers after a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A washtub is a large tub used for washing clothes, a vessel for cleaning.

clue.text: Ancient coin southern engineer found under compound

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under something means coming after it in the column

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
an ester is a chemical compound
CE stands for civil engineer

explanation.surface: An old coin turned up by an engineer in the south, buried beneath an enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: S comes first, then the engineer sits under the compound in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: The sesterce, or sestertius, was a small coin of ancient Rome.

clue.text: German philosopher's ailment UK man treated

indicators.note: something treated is processed or worked on, so these letters are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A British man treated a German thinker for an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'has', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Immanuel Kant was the eighteenth-century German philosopher who wrote the Critique of Pure Reason.

clue.text: Curtailed the strange monotonous sound

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short at the tail, so the last letter of the following word is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
rum is an old informal word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: An odd droning noise was cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrum is a continuous low humming or strumming noise, a monotonous sound.

clue.text: Early Egyptian king initially relished cooked sesame

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it attaches to
cooked food is mixed and changed, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: first letter of relished
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient pharaoh enjoyed a dish made with sesame.
explanation.definitionFit: Rameses (Ramesses) was the name of several pharaohs of ancient Egypt, rulers in an early civilisation.

clue.text: Unmarried girl with rook finding English hillfort

blocks.note: a maiden is an unmarried young woman
in chess the rook is also called the castle

explanation.surface: A single young woman and a crow discover an ancient earthwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' suggests the bird, but it is the chess piece. Maiden Castle is a huge Iron Age hillfort in Dorset.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiden Castle near Dorchester is one of the largest Iron Age earthwork forts in England.

clue.text: Stalwart sore after playing musical instrument

indicators.note: playing about with something moves it around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a lute is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: A determined musician feels sore after a long performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' reads as part of the order of pieces, yet the rearranged word comes first; it simply means the soreness follows the playing.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalwart and resolute both describe someone firm, loyal and determined.

clue.text: At the end, notable player posed with unknown substitute

indicators.note: at the end directs us to the final letter of each of the following two words

blocks.note: last letters of notable and player
to pose for a portrait is to sit, past tense sat
z is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A star player ends up sitting out alongside an unknown replacement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notable player' reads as one celebrated performer, but it only supplies the two last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior imitation used in place of the real thing, a substitute.

clue.text: Cocktail party above saloon perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, above means the first piece sits higher in the column, so it comes first

blocks.note: a side is a party in a dispute or contest
a saloon is a type of car, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: A drinks party upstairs from a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon' suggests a bar beside 'Cocktail', but here it is a car body style.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Somewhere in Canada, plaque becomes visible somewhat

indicators.note: something partly visible shows only a portion, so the letters lie inside the neighbouring words

blocks.note: read straight through the middle of these two words

explanation.surface: A commemorative plaque is uncovered somewhere in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Quebec is a province, and a city, in eastern Canada.

clue.text: Bringer of bad luck ultimately avoided carrying a new piano

indicators.note: the final letter is the one avoided, so the word loses its end
carrying means holding, so the shortened word wraps the next pieces

blocks.note: a Jonah is someone thought to bring bad luck, after the biblical prophet
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A jinx narrowly misses being hit by a new piano being carried.
explanation.walkthrough: Joanna is Cockney rhyming slang for piano (pronounced 'pianna').
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a joanna is a piano, from its rhyme with the dialect pronunciation.

clue.text: Antique coach given to couple — it might represent preferential treatment

blocks.note: antique means old
to coach someone is to school or train them
to couple things is to tie them together

explanation.surface: An old stagecoach is handed to a pair, perhaps as a favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' suggests a vehicle beside 'Antique', but it is the verb to train.
explanation.definitionFit: The old school tie stands for the network of former pupils of the same school favouring one another.

clue.text: Some final lessons? Everything considered

indicators.note: some means a portion only, so the letters are part of the words that follow

blocks.note: read straight through these two words

explanation.surface: A student wonders whether there are any last classes, taking everything into account.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'in all' means in total or taking everything together.

clue.text: River erosion

blocks.note: first meaning: the river that flows through Durham in northeast England
second meaning: gradual damage from use or friction

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like riverbank erosion; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wear is an English river, and wear is the gradual deterioration of a surface through friction.

clue.text: Relative emptied out Austin that's dirty

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving just its outer letters

blocks.note: an uncle is a relative
first and last letters of Austin

explanation.surface: A relative cleared out a filthy old Austin car.
explanation.walkthrough: Austin reads as a classic British car make, but only its outside letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean is a direct synonym of dirty, meaning not clean or soiled.

clue.text: Open-mouthed, Georgia's overwhelmed by primate

indicators.note: being overwhelmed by something means being engulfed by it, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: an ape is a primate
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Someone from Georgia gapes in shock at being overpowered by an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: Agape means with the mouth wide open, as in wonder or surprise.

clue.text: One that can hear large aristocrat

blocks.note: the ear is the organ of hearing; that the letters also run through 'hear large' is a coincidence
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A big nobleman who is not deaf.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman ranking above a viscount, so an aristocrat.

clue.text: Old rebel leader, terribly disheartened, left in rain?

indicators.note: disheartened means with the heart removed, so only the outer letters of the word stay
in places the preceding letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: rain is an example of water, hence the question mark
first and last letters of terribly
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A rebel chief, badly downhearted, is left out in the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: Wat Tyler led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381 in England; the question mark flags rain as just one example of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Wat Tyler was the leader of the English Peasants' Revolt in 1381, an old-time rebel chief.
